catalog.summary: Digital organisms with genome architecture evolve through mutation, reproduction, competition, and environmental selection.
catalog.verification_note: Official model description and analysis tools reviewed.
catalog.correction: A fixed-target characterization is too broad: platform supports controlled environmental variation and extensions.

catalog.summary: Artificial chemistry applies lambda expressions to one another, producing computational reaction networks and self-organized organizations.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' 2024 replication-study abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Cited paper revisits 1990s work; label source as a replication rather than the original 1994 publication. Robustness is qualified by observed fragility.

catalog.summary: CUDA simulation and rendering combine soft-body and fluid dynamics, genomes, neural networks, and ecosystem tools.
catalog.verification_note: Official feature list and release notes reviewed.
catalog.correction: Current feature documentation supports mechanisms, not sustained open-ended evolution, consciousness, or claimed superiority scores.

catalog.summary: Random machine-instruction sequences can self-organize into self-replicating programs in a computationally universal instruction environment.
catalog.verification_note: Original Pargellis 2001 paper abstract reviewed after publisher access failed.
catalog.correction: Use the verified paper record; emergence of replication is distinct from unlimited evolutionary innovation.

catalog.summary: Early computational model represents component production and boundary maintenance in a spatial particle system.
catalog.verification_note: 2004 review citation reviewed; original 1974 repository paper found but blocked by access challenge. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Input URL is McMullin's review, not the original paper. Self-maintenance does not imply offspring production; primary details require further review.

catalog.summary: Self-replicating digital organisms evolve through mutation, selection, and drift in controlled computational experiments.
catalog.verification_note: Maintainer repository and Ofria/Wilke primary paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Capabilities vary by experiment; instrumented digital evolution is not an unconditional proof of open-endedness.

catalog.summary: Colored segment-based organisms mutate and evolve in a two-dimensional simulation inspired by Primordial Life.
catalog.verification_note: Maintainer project description reviewed; manual fetch timed out.
catalog.correction: Compare inherited morphology and ecological interactions; do not infer cognition from evolving shapes.

catalog.summary: Plant-like cellular-automaton organisms grow from seeds, compete for nutrients and reproduce with variation in simulated biomes.
catalog.verification_note: Original 2023 paper abstract and author project article reviewed.
catalog.correction: A close comparator for coupled development, resource flows and reproduction; stability depends on configuration.

catalog.summary: Genomes specify neural controllers for agents in a two-dimensional grid, with configurable generational selection and signals.
catalog.verification_note: README describes genome-to-network conversion, sensors, selection, and pheromone layer.
catalog.correction: Evolved neural wiring is not evidence of lifetime synaptic learning; claims depend on configured selection scenario.

catalog.summary: Local separation, alignment, and cohesion rules generate coordinated flocking; additional steering behaviors support obstacle avoidance.
catalog.verification_note: Creator Craig Reynolds explicitly dates model creation to 1986 and conference publication to 1987.
catalog.correction: Collective motion is not by itself a food web, reproduction mechanism, or learned policy.

catalog.summary: Local graph-rewrite systems exhibit persistent, multiplying and terminating structures in experiments inspired by artificial chemistry and lambda calculus.
catalog.verification_note: Author's 2020 experimental notes abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Computational graph replication does not by itself establish Darwinian ecology or biological metabolism.

catalog.summary: Artificial-life world supports experiments on proposed conditions for open-ended evolution, with evidence discussed in Soros's doctoral dissertation.
catalog.verification_note: Author's institutional dissertation abstract and 2018 metadata reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Tests of necessary conditions do not prove sufficient conditions or indefinitely sustained open-endedness.

catalog.summary: Ventrella's asymmetric particle-interaction simulation produces self-organized collective patterns from species-dependent motion rules.
catalog.verification_note: Author's live project page reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Clusters inspired Tom Mohr's Particle Life; the names are not exact aliases. Canonicalize to Clusters and record lineage.

catalog.summary: Two-state cellular automaton whose local birth and survival rules support complex patterns and engineered computation.
catalog.verification_note: Read the reproduced October 1970 Gardner introduction.
catalog.correction: Pattern multiplication and universal computation do not establish Darwinian evolution or general cognition.

catalog.summary: Programs written in Redcode compete for survival in shared virtual memory under a specified interpreter.
catalog.verification_note: Read Jones and Dewdney's March 1984 original implementation guidelines.
catalog.correction: Original source was a 2026 Digital Red Queen paper. Core War itself is a competitive programming arena; evolutionary training belongs to particular extensions.

catalog.summary: Tim Taylor and John Hallam's self-replicating-program system extends Tierra with simplified cellular-organism modeling.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' 1997 abstract and bibliographic entry reviewed.
catalog.correction: Exploring multicellularity is a research aim, not evidence that a Cambrian-style transition was achieved.

catalog.summary: Swimmers evolve anatomy and motion across generations in an interactive artificial-life pond.
catalog.verification_note: Creator page confirms 1996 research origin and 1997 product development.
catalog.correction: Separate research start from release; retain as precursor to Gene Pool, not an alias of it.

catalog.summary: Program-controlled organisms feed, reproduce and mutate in a continuous two-dimensional world.
catalog.verification_note: Original author project page; historical version.
catalog.correction: No fixed external fitness target does not by itself establish sustained open-ended evolution.

catalog.summary: Self-replicating digital cells form cooperative groups, share resources and coordinate behavior through evolved event-driven programs.
catalog.verification_note: Author methods, experiment design and knockout results reviewed.
catalog.correction: A direct comparator for cooperation and transitions in individuality; results depend on the specified environment.

catalog.summary: Physically simulated blocks grow, divide, form joints and exchange resources under evolved recurrent neural controllers in a solar-energy environment.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' project page and paper abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Source describes approximately conserved energy and preliminary cooperative resource transactions; preserve those qualifications.

catalog.summary: Holland's model uses interacting, resource-dependent agents to explore adaptation and organization.
catalog.verification_note: Author's publication list and Smith/Bedau paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: The cited 2000 study concludes that tested Echo runs lacked the diversity of hierarchical aggregates characteristic of complex adaptive systems; it is not blanket validation.

catalog.summary: Peter Krčah's reimplementation evolves virtual-creature morphology and controllers for walking and swimming using ODE physics.
catalog.verification_note: Read Krčah's original GECCO 2007 paper.
catalog.correction: Original source was wrong: 493.pdf is Vít Růžička's 2014 Framsticks bachelor's thesis. Correct author is Peter Krčah.

catalog.summary: Ken Stauffer's artificial-life simulator models evolving program-controlled organisms; the linked repository preserves a later fork.
catalog.verification_note: Repository identity, author attribution, and project structure reviewed.
catalog.correction: Do not describe a 12-commit historical fork as maintained without release/activity evidence.

catalog.summary: A mass-conserving Lenia extension localizes update parameters, enabling coexisting patterns and parameter mixing.
catalog.verification_note: Original abstract distinguishes demonstrations from a proposed route toward intrinsic evolution.
catalog.correction: Use Flow-Lenia as canonical spelling; do not convert future potential into achieved open-ended evolution.

catalog.summary: A simulation platform models creature bodies and neural controllers, supporting optimization, coevolution, and ecological experiments.
catalog.verification_note: Creator site and tutorial describe body/controller models and configurable experiments.
catalog.correction: A platform's support for an experiment does not prove that every run exhibits its target behavior.

catalog.summary: An artificial-chemistry model studies mutually catalytic molecular assemblies, compositional inheritance and growth followed by division.
catalog.verification_note: Original paper indexed abstract reviewed; full-page fetch hit a browser challenge.
catalog.correction: Compositional heredity differs from sequence copying; broad evolvability claims need separate evidence.

catalog.summary: A biotically selected neural-agent system studies long-term evolutionary activity and scaling of individual complexity.
catalog.verification_note: Read Channon's 2019 abstract, including experimental bounds and scaling result.
catalog.correction: The result is qualified by evaluated run scales and requires scaling both world size and neural limits. Remove timeless 'only besides Earth' superlative.

catalog.summary: Swimbots inhabit an interactive pond with food, mutation, reproduction, and selectable mate preferences.
catalog.verification_note: Live creator interface exposes mutation, offspring energy, food, and mate-preference controls.
catalog.correction: Gene Pool and Swimbots refer to one catalog entry; 1997 origin was not independently established in the reviewed page.

catalog.summary: Simulation evolves body and controller designs that are transferred into fabricated locomoting robots.
catalog.verification_note: Read original Lipson and Pollack paper.
catalog.correction: Automated design and fabrication pipeline is not autonomous robot self-reproduction; assembly and manufacturing interventions matter.

catalog.summary: Neural-network-controlled agents evolve in a world with programmable robots; the authors analyze communication, agriculture and tool use.
catalog.verification_note: Original 2024 paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Reported emergent behaviors are experimental findings; an open-ended title does not prove indefinitely increasing complexity.

catalog.summary: Particle automata with discrete internal states and continuous simulated physics assemble into self-replicating strings.
catalog.verification_note: Original 2002 author paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Particle-mediated replication is a useful contrast to program-level fission; it does not establish unbounded evolution.

catalog.summary: Evolutionary algorithms co-design block-based morphology and control for tasks including swimming, walking, and competition.
catalog.verification_note: Creator's 1994 project page describes selection, recombination, mutation, and task-based experiments.
catalog.correction: Keep fitness-driven body/control evolution distinct from self-reproduction occurring inside a persistent ecosystem.

catalog.summary: A rule-following agent changes grid states while moving, producing complex trajectories from simple local rules.
catalog.verification_note: Langton's 1986 original paper identified in university repository.
catalog.correction: The ant is a programmed dynamical system; the familiar highway does not imply learning or evolution.

catalog.summary: A cellular-automaton loop copies its circulating description to construct further loops.
catalog.verification_note: Original 1984 article abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Self-reproduction does not require universal construction; standard loop copying should not be scored as demonstrated adaptive evolution.

catalog.summary: Long-range Life-like cellular automata generalize the neighborhood of the original rule.
catalog.verification_note: Pivato's paper explicitly credits K. M. Evans for Larger than Life and proves a continuum-limit result.
catalog.correction: Correct attribution: the cited RealLife paper is by Marcus Pivato, not Evans.

catalog.summary: Continuous cellular automata support localized patterns with movement, self-organization, and other life-like dynamics.
catalog.verification_note: Creator synopsis and timeline reviewed.
catalog.correction: Project began in 2015; 2018 refers to initial public paper/video. Later extensions include replication-like behavior; version must be specified.

catalog.summary: A compact artificial-life virtual machine supports interacting program-like organisms; the cited fork modifies instructions, energy limits, and statistics.

catalog.summary: An extension of Tierra distributes digital-organism populations across networked environments.
catalog.verification_note: Creator site separately links Network Tierra, FAQ, and net/non-net release.
catalog.correction: Retain as a Tierra extension with shared family; do not count it as wholly unrelated or infer evolved multicellularity from its name.

catalog.summary: Learned local update rules act on moving particles using differentiable SPH operators, supporting morphogenesis and regeneration.
catalog.verification_note: Author abstract and revision history reviewed; 2026 preprint.
catalog.correction: Learned morphogenesis is distinct from hereditary reproduction and ecological selection.

catalog.summary: A particle-based reformulation explores Lenia-like self-organizing patterns.
catalog.verification_note: Creator tutorial identity confirmed; JavaScript notebook content was not fully exposed by text retrieval.

catalog.summary: Interactive two-dimensional ant simulation demonstrates local movement and marker-mediated foraging in environments with food and obstacles.
catalog.verification_note: Public repository and controls reviewed; channel-wide source narrowed to a specific repository, attribution supported by linked creator context. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Original row points to an entire YouTube channel. Version and implementation must be pinned; no neural-learning claim established.

catalog.summary: An artificial-life research environment couples evolving organisms, neural controllers, and ecological interactions.
catalog.verification_note: Read repository README attributed to Larry Yaeger and collaborator history.
catalog.correction: The linked repository is an old copy, not evidence of a currently maintained release; no current version benchmark was run.

catalog.summary: Educational simulation videos illustrate how resource competition and inherited variation affect populations over generations.
catalog.verification_note: Author's indexed video metadata and description reviewed; full simulation code and detailed mechanics not independently inspected. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.

catalog.summary: Self-propelled particles under a simple interaction law form structures that grow, divide, and interact.
catalog.verification_note: Read original 2016 paper abstract and publication metadata.
catalog.correction: Emergent cell-like reproduction is reported; genome-based heredity and sustained adaptive novelty require separate evidence.

catalog.summary: A one-dimensional binary cellular automaton supports universal computation under carefully constructed initial conditions.
catalog.verification_note: Cook's primary explanatory paper and original 2004 publication identified.

catalog.summary: Related cellular-automata systems add structural dissolution to replicating loops; Evoloop additionally supports heritable variation through interactions and selection.

catalog.summary: Educational simulation explores rabbit and fox populations, resources, inherited traits, and survival tradeoffs.
catalog.verification_note: Author video description reviewed; Ecosystem-2 repository identifies itself as a work-in-progress follow-up. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.

catalog.summary: Gradient-based optimization and curriculum exploration discover robust moving, self-maintaining patterns in continuous cellular automata.
catalog.verification_note: Authors explain the method and link its extended Science Advances publication.
catalog.correction: A distinct research extension within the Lenia family; trained robustness is not a proof of lifetime learning or consciousness.

catalog.summary: A continuous-domain generalization of Conway's Life supports smooth dynamical patterns.
catalog.verification_note: Rafler's original 2011 abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Pattern dynamics alone do not establish heredity, selection, or cognition.

catalog.summary: An artificial chemistry models interacting particles and evolvable self-replicating molecular structures.
catalog.verification_note: Creator repository identifies the artificial-chemistry implementation and links its project.
catalog.correction: A single artificial chemistry is not multiple physical substrates; detailed paper claims were not fully replicated.

catalog.summary: Opcode-string molecules bind probabilistically and execute reactions, enabling studies of replication, mutation and evolving molecular interactions.
catalog.verification_note: Researchers' analysis repository and linked research citations reviewed alongside ISAL explanatory entry. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Source supports study of evolved replication; remove unconditional claims that open-endedness is settled or universally quantified.

catalog.summary: An agent-based artificial society studies how local interactions generate population-level social patterns.
catalog.verification_note: Publisher confirms Epstein and Axtell book and October 1996 publication.
catalog.correction: Detailed model configurations vary; do not assign all book experiments to every Sugarscape implementation.

catalog.summary: Heterogeneous self-propelled particles follow local kinetic rules, producing collective structures; extensions study evolutionary swarm dynamics.
catalog.verification_note: Author's homepage, descriptions and publication links reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Separate original interactive Swarm Chemistry from later Evolutionary Swarm Chemistry capabilities.

catalog.summary: Artificial-life simulation evolves digital creatures with genetic traits and neural controllers in a resource-based environment.
catalog.verification_note: Official site reviewed; creator dates project to 2017. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Creator's ambitions and promotional language are not evidence of limitless behavior, consciousness, or biologically equivalent life.

catalog.summary: Cellular artificial-life simulator lets organisms eat, reproduce, mutate and compete, with selection arising from survival and offspring production.
catalog.verification_note: Author repository README reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Natural-selection design is documented; sustained unbounded novelty remains a separate empirical claim.

catalog.summary: Self-replicating programs compete for computational resources and undergo mutation in a virtual environment.
catalog.verification_note: Creator's site identifies Tierra and links software, documentation, and Network Tierra.
catalog.correction: Use creator's site instead of course mirror; do not infer sustained unbounded innovation from digital evolution alone.

catalog.summary: A four-state cellular automaton models moving signals in conductors and can implement logic circuits.
catalog.verification_note: Implementation documentation and Wolfram's research book examples reviewed.
catalog.correction: Evidence concerns circuit computation; neither intelligence nor biological reproduction follows from universality.

catalog.summary: Foundation models guide searches across artificial-life simulators for target behavior, novelty, and diverse patterns.
catalog.verification_note: Original Sakana research announcement dated December 24, 2024 reviewed.
catalog.correction: ASAL is a discovery method spanning multiple simulators; its search algorithm and discovered worlds should not be conflated.

catalog.summary: Meta-agent search generates and evaluates agent programs, retaining prior designs to inform subsequent discoveries.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: An automated design method, not a population of metabolizing autonomous organisms.

catalog.summary: Foundation-model-driven search modifies coding-agent programs, evaluates changes on coding benchmarks, and accumulates an archive of agent variants.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract, benchmark figures and version history reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Title is not evidence for a maximum OEE score. Benchmark improvement and growing archives do not prove indefinite innovation.

catalog.summary: Evolution searches articulated morphologies while reinforcement learning trains control, studying embodiment and learnability across environments.
catalog.verification_note: Original paper identifies DERL and links the same Nature DOI used in the input.
catalog.correction: Merge UNIMAL row into this entry: UNIMAL is the design space in the same framework, not an independent comparison project.

catalog.summary: LLM-driven self-play evolves Core War programs against previous opponents, studying adaptation to a changing adversarial objective.
catalog.verification_note: Original January 2026 paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Distinct method built on Core War; it is not the 1984 Core War source and not evidence of unbounded innovation.

catalog.summary: Boundedly rational agents select attendance predictions and decide whether to visit a bar, creating collective congestion dynamics.
catalog.verification_note: Official implementation documentation reviewed; cites Arthur's 1994 paper and distinguishes its revised strategy representation. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Predictor switching is adaptation; do not describe every implementation as genetic evolution.

catalog.summary: Co-generates learning challenges and agents, allowing solution transfer among tasks and measuring exploration progress.
catalog.verification_note: Original 2020 paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Evidence concerns the reported algorithm and experiments; a title containing unbounded does not establish limitless real-world novelty.

catalog.summary: An extension infers hidden-neuron placement and density from an indirect connectivity encoding.
catalog.verification_note: Original Risi and Stanley 2012 abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: A distinct HyperNEAT extension, not an independent organism world; finite experiments do not establish unrestricted complexity growth.

catalog.summary: Code language models supply mutation operators within evolutionary search, demonstrated on programs that generate Sodarace walkers.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Algorithmic inheritance in search is distinct from autonomous in-world reproduction; linked to OpenELM implementation family.

catalog.summary: Evolution combines generative encodings and multiple voxel materials to discover locomoting soft-body robot designs.
catalog.verification_note: Original GECCO 2013 paper identified and abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Input DOI points to a 2014 SIGEVOlution version; original experiment appeared at GECCO 2013. This is externally optimized design, not ecological reproduction.

catalog.summary: Genesys evolves bit-string-encoded programs, including finite-state and neural controllers, with Tracker studying behavior on an artificial-ant task.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' original paper introduction reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Task-specific evolutionary optimization does not imply lifetime learning or open-ended ecology; different controller encodings are alternatives.

catalog.summary: Exploration algorithms archive promising states, return to them, and explore further; demonstrated on sparse-reward games and robotic tasks.
catalog.verification_note: Author abstract reviewed; Nature endpoint failed, replaced with authors' preprint. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Exploration performance does not establish indefinitely sustained open-ended evolution.

catalog.summary: An indirect encoding generates neural connectivity from geometric patterns, exploiting symmetry and repeated structure.
catalog.verification_note: Original Stanley, D'Ambrosio, and Gauci 2009 manuscript reviewed.
catalog.correction: Retain as a distinct algorithm in the NEAT family; avoid scoring interchangeable computational encodings as physical substrate diversity.

catalog.summary: Deep-network assessments guide divergent evolutionary search for recognizable artifacts; the original demonstration generates images.
catalog.verification_note: Author-hosted 2015 paper abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Original paper distinguishes a long-term vision from a simplified implemented demonstration.

catalog.summary: An archive retains high-performing solutions across user-chosen behavioral or phenotypic descriptor regions.
catalog.verification_note: Original Mouret and Clune 2015 abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Quality-diversity coverage is not unlimited open-ended evolution; descriptor dimensions and evaluation rules are supplied.

catalog.summary: Maze populations and navigating agents coevolve under minimal success criteria, producing diverse maze structures and agent behaviors.
catalog.verification_note: Institutional record reproduces the authors' abstract, authors and 2017 GECCO citation. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: The abstract calls this a step toward open-ended algorithms; 'indefinitely growing complexity' exceeds the evidence.

catalog.summary: An evolutionary algorithm optimizes neural weights and topology using speciation, structural innovation tracking, and incremental complexification.
catalog.verification_note: Read original 2002 paper abstract and mechanism claims.
catalog.correction: An algorithm does not intrinsically have ecology, reproduction in a world, or visual scale; these are application-dependent.

catalog.summary: A graph neural network uses an agent's body structure to parameterize a continuous-control policy.
catalog.verification_note: Original paper indexed text reviewed; direct OpenReview access hit browser verification.
catalog.correction: Policy architecture alone is not an evolved body or complete artificial-life ecosystem.

catalog.summary: Evolutionary graph search designs robots while graph-network controllers transfer skills among candidate bodies.
catalog.verification_note: Original 2019 paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Selection and mutation occur in a design algorithm; do not conflate with autonomous physical self-reproduction.

catalog.summary: Evolutionary search rewards behavioral novelty instead of direct objective progress.
catalog.verification_note: Original Lehman and Stanley 2011 paper abstract reviewed.
catalog.correction: Novelty search can explore without a task objective, but novelty metrics and representation constrain results.

catalog.project: OMNI (Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness)

catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract and version history reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Task generation is not organism reproduction; no universal OEE score follows from the title.

catalog.summary: Foundation models generate environment and reward code for tasks selected to be interesting and appropriate to agents' capabilities.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract and version history reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: A distinct extension of OMNI in the same family; in-principle unrestricted task generation does not prove indefinite realized novelty.

catalog.summary: Evolutionary procedure adapts task prompts and the mutation prompts used to generate their variants.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Optimization over task prompts has fixed evaluation domains; distinguish prompt evolution from organism self-replication.

catalog.summary: Language models generate variations and assess quality and diversity within an evolutionary search over creative text.
catalog.verification_note: Authors' abstract reviewed, including comparison with human evaluations. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Coverage of a specified search space is not unrestricted open-ended evolution.

catalog.summary: Graph grammars define robot structures, and heuristic search optimizes designs and controllers for terrain tasks.
catalog.verification_note: Original authors' indexed project page and paper metadata reviewed; old CDFG URL redirected to a large publication index.
catalog.correction: Replace unstable generic redirect with specific project page; an optimizer is not a self-maintaining ecosystem.

catalog.summary: Local relocation decisions based on neighborhood composition can produce large-scale segregation without equally strong individual preferences.
catalog.verification_note: Original publisher abstract and NetLogo implementation documentation reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: A foundational social model, not an evolving organism platform; implementations are variants of one model family.

catalog.summary: A graph-based policy first modifies body structure and then controls the resulting agent, jointly optimizing morphology and behavior.
catalog.verification_note: Original abstract and submission history reviewed.
catalog.correction: 2021 preprint; ICLR 2022 publication. Learned design actions are not organism reproduction.

catalog.summary: A theoretical cellular-automaton construction separates a machine's description, interpretation, and copying to enable self-reproduction.
catalog.verification_note: Original book scan identified; full browser retrieval exceeded size limit.
catalog.correction: Distinguish 1940s-1950s work from the posthumous 1966 publication; the constructor alone and complete reproducer are different components.

catalog.summary: A Julia framework supports discrete-time and event-based agent models with spatial environments, analysis tools and ecosystem examples.
catalog.verification_note: Official introduction and example index reviewed.
catalog.correction: Separate framework features from the ecological or learning behavior of an individual model.

catalog.summary: A modular multi-physics simulator supports experiments with large robot swarms and configurable robot and physics plugins.
catalog.verification_note: Official definition and documentation index reviewed.
catalog.correction: A swarm-robotics comparator; robot population size alone is not evolutionary or ecological complexity.

catalog.summary: Agent-based modeling framework built around composable scapes, with facilities for rules, visualization, statistics, and experiments.

catalog.summary: Educational software lets users design experiments with evolving digital organisms and inspect results.

catalog.summary: An open-source platform supports creation, execution and visualization of agent-based simulations, including biological and ecological models.

catalog.verification_note: Publisher product page reviewed. Review covers identity and conservative description, not an independent runtime reproduction.
catalog.correction: Player-guided creature design is not evidence of autonomous Darwinian evolution; avoid declaring absence of all inheritance mechanisms.

repository_audit.working_tree_status: unconfirmed: status returned not-in-work-tree; bundled Git chdir returned permission denied
repository_audit.scope: Read-only inspection of selected current working files; no suite or simulator executed, no repository edits; arithmetic recomputed independently in Python. HEAD is a reference, not assurance all inspected files equal committed content.

claims.finding: Browser-hosted artificial-life and cognitive-mechanism research testbed with multiple interacting numerical models. The repository is a prototype; source breadth is not evidence of scientific superiority.
EntityManager implements asexual inheritance and bounded point mutation of nW, strategy, typeId and setGroup. The auto-fission probability is 0.02 + 0.08*clamp01(nW), with trait-blind 0.06 ablation.
claims.qualification: This supports gene-linked fecundity in a bounded simulated population; not instruction-level self-replication, sexual genome evolution or independently replicated multi-generational ecology. Gate source inspected, not executed.

claims.finding: The shipped fecundity objective is monotonic in nW and has a fixed optimum at nW=1. The current scoring script explicitly corrects earlier claims of a GA in emergence-angles, inherited petri selection and fitness-weighted soup parenthood.
claims.qualification: No demonstrated sustained open-ended evolution. Authoring new mechanisms or producing novelty does not establish unbounded adaptive innovation.

claims.finding: Repository documents edible flora, grazing/waste/fertilizer feedback, predation, weather and a sanctuary. The refuge test uses four comparison arms and a direct immunity ablation, while holding the sanctuary percept coupling.
claims.qualification: A modeled food web with authored rules, not real-world ecological fidelity or verified autonomous plant-genome coevolution. Numerical population outcomes in comments were not rerun. The scoring-script prose describing withholding safeZoneAt is stale relative to the stronger current immunity ablation test.

claims.finding: Docs describe Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion, state-driven geometry and shaders, and soft plant interaction.
claims.qualification: Reactive morphology is not equivalent to evolution of articulated body plans in a physics simulator such as Sims or Framsticks. No benchmarked morphology superiority established.

claims.finding: The repository contains bounded numerical policies, prediction-error control, chemotaxis, parameter-shift VQE drive resolution and predictive-metacognition modules with focused ablation tests. Xylos adds recurrent numerical sensing and action.
claims.qualification: These are different mechanisms, not a calibrated intelligence scale. Later V4 and Phase-B reports retain failed controls and forbid broad intelligence/learning/scaling uplift.

claims.finding: Current canonical docs retain V4 failures for ordinary organisms, predictor and Petri; Titans pass only bounded game-policy semantic causality. Phase-B V3 predictor fails all advancement criteria; narrow NHI action diagnostics do not authorize adaptation or broad learning claims.
claims.qualification: Repository-reported experimental receipts; not rerun or independently replicated in this audit.

claims.finding: Xenomimic source contains classical numerical statevectors and a numerical position-space Schrodinger solver; wavepacket spread changes a control signal.
claims.qualification: No physical QPU, quantum hardware advantage, physical quantum entropy, or quantum consciousness demonstrated. Multiple simulated model families share classical digital hardware. A count of consumers or numerical formalisms is not physical substrate diversity; rename this axis to model/integration diversity if retained.

claims.finding: A dedicated seeded mulberry32 sample is passed through a statistical randomness battery; it does not tap or perturb live draws. Source exposes sample count, entropy, serial correlation and monobit statistic.
claims.qualification: Statistical diagnostics on a pseudorandom generator do not certify cryptographic randomness or physical entropy. Test count/coverage are repository receipts, not scientific validity.

claims.finding: Kernel snapshots explicitly carry indicatorOnly. Canonical docs say 8/14 met plus 6/14 partial, and report weak coupling and a near-zero lab null gap.
claims.qualification: The 8+6 result is a project-specific architectural assessment, not external certification or proof of consciousness. Xylos has a separate research-target table; apex assessment does not transfer.

claims.finding: Xylos is a compact recurrent autonomous numeric organism with chemistry sensing, plastic coupling, visible neural state and bounded local input recording/replay. Live mode injects browser entropy; seeded mode is reproducible.
claims.qualification: Replay reconstructs the brain input trajectory, not whole-world rollback. Live entropy cannot be regenerated from seed alone. No tokens/network inference required. No consciousness, general intelligence or open-ended biological evolution established.

claims.finding: README describes 10k default population and 50k explicit stress ceiling; current metadata version is 0.23.0 and canonical tracked-suite receipt is 3381.
claims.qualification: The scoring script records roughly 167 ms/frame for a historical 50k benchmark; do not market 50k as demonstrated smooth interactive performance. Suite not run in this audit; no independent replication evidence located.
